citation: Levy (2026), Caution Ahead: Numerical Reasoning and Look-Ahead Bias in AI Models, Journal of Accounting Research 64(3), 1139-1188; published HTML read
text_source: Compustat annual statements 1968-2021 as anonymous Markdown tables with relative year labels (no name, no date, no text); 346,731 firm-years, LLM tests on about 1,900
feature: LLM call on raw statements versus statements with 1, 3 or 5 trailing digits randomised or all items scaled by 1,000
method: Chain-of-thought prompt to gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, gpt-4-0125-preview, gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18; 410M-parameter models with yearly cutoffs 1999-2023; rolling GBDT benchmark
outcome: Direction of next-year net income (accuracy, F1, AUC)
incremental_to: Base rate of increases (0.58); GBDT on the same items (accuracy 0.627, AUC 0.652)
pit_handling: Tests recall directly: gpt-4 accuracy 0.60 to 0.51 with one digit randomised and 0.51 when scaled; GBDT 0.627 to 0.623; own models predict only when the cutoff is after the statement year; no firm or year identification test; argues vendor cutoffs are optimistic
informs_decision: S2 strategy A (smallest perturbation that breaks recall); blind PM judged against a statistical baseline; arithmetic in code; perturbation invariance as a leakage metric (strategy B use 2); margin after cutoff under rule 2

citation: Engelberg, Manela, Mullins and Vulicevic (2025), Entity Neutering, working paper, SSRN 5182756; draft of 26 June 2026 read from the PDF linked on Mullins's page
text_source: Dow Jones news 2000-2022 (509,719 articles); 102,070 MD&A sections 2002-2023; 11,411 earnings call transcripts 2017-2024
feature: LLM sentiment (direction and magnitude) from raw text versus text masked and paraphrased until a fresh LLM cannot name the firm or date
method: Iterative mask, identify, paraphrase, identify with gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07 (9 rounds news, 20 MD&A); identified texts dropped; panel regressions, calendar-time alphas, bound on look-ahead share
horizon: Day t+1 and days t+2 to t+5
incremental_to: Raw-text sentiment; Loughran-McDonald and Garcia et al. dictionaries; Tetlock-style controls; six factors
pit_handling: Firm named 69.1% and date 92.5% with name-only masking, 47.3% with Glasserman-Lin masking, 0.11% and 0.03% after neutering (chance 0.11%); large firms 0.24%; all numbers replaced by placeholders; 16.3% of articles lose sentiment; all samples pre-cutoff; attackers are small models
informs_decision: S2 strategy A with an LLM (rewriting removes the numbers that are our label); H2 (date leaks more than name under light masking); strategy C (drop what stays identifiable); attacker prompt and chance benchmarks; megacap bottleneck

citation: Jeon and Lee (2026), Can Blindfolded LLMs Still Trade? An Anonymization-First Framework for Portfolio Optimization, arXiv 2603.17692 v1 (ICLR 2026 FinAI workshop)
text_source: Point-in-time S&P 500 constituents 2020-01 to 2025-08; technical indicators and up to 5 anonymised headlines per stock
feature: Scores and reasoning embeddings from four Gemini 2.5 Flash agents on inputs with tickers and names replaced by synthetic identifiers
method: Agent scores into a graph attention network and a PPO policy (top 20, no cash, 10 bps costs); rank IC screen; cross-sectional shuffle as negative control
outcome: Portfolio Sharpe ratio and cumulative return; rank IC with forward returns
horizon: Daily rebalancing; IC at 21 trading days
incremental_to: SPY, equal weight, momentum, largest 20, raw-indicator top 20; ablation without LLM features
pit_handling: Renaming plus a cutoff instruction; decision date shown to the model; no identification test and no raw-ticker arm (authors: anonymisation effect not directly validated); model cutoff not stated; point-in-time index membership
informs_decision: S2 strategy A (renaming untested, so no support); do not show the date (H2); a shuffle test is a sanity check and not a leakage metric

citation: Glasserman and Lin (2023), Assessing Look-Ahead Bias in Stock Return Predictions Generated by GPT Sentiment Analysis, arXiv 2309.17322 v1
text_source: News headlines 2015-2022: 129,431 web-scraped (6,723 firms) and 181,908 Thomson Reuters (678 S&P 500 firms)
feature: GPT-3.5 sentiment score (+1, 0, -1) on original headlines versus headlines with the company name, abbreviation and up to 20 Knowledge Graph products replaced by a fixed string
method: Daily equal-weighted long-short portfolios; paired t-tests; stacked regressions with firm and time fixed effects and a Wald test
outcome: Next-period stock return (open to close or close to close)
pit_handling: In-sample (to September 2021) versus out-of-sample (October 2021 to December 2022) by vendor cutoff; replaced beats original in-sample (Thomson Reuters 13.84 v 10.74 bp, p = 0.017) and borderline out-of-sample (p = 0.064); no identification test; dates and numbers left in
informs_decision: Raw-versus-blind gap is not a leakage measure (distraction effect); agreement with the raw call is not pure fidelity; a name-driven prior exists and is larger for big firms; renaming unsupported on text

citation: Kim, Muhn and Nikolaev (2024), Financial Statement Analysis with Large Language Models, arXiv 2407.17866; v2 of November 2024 read in part; withdrawn by the authors in v3 (February 2025)
text_source: Compustat annual statements 1968-2021, standardised, names removed and years relabelled t and t-1; 150,678 firm-years
feature: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0125-preview) chain-of-thought forecast from the two statements
method: Simple and chain-of-thought prompts compared with analysts, stepwise logit and neural networks trained on rolling five-year windows
incremental_to: Analyst forecasts (53%), stepwise logit (52.94%), ANN (60.45%); GPT 60.31%
pit_handling: Anonymised inputs; model asked to guess firm and year (0.07% and 2.95% correct); a 2023 out-of-sample test; authors conclude no memory; withdrawn for inconsistencies in data and analyses
informs_decision: The setting Levy (2026) appears to re-create without naming it; an identification rate near zero does not rule out recall, so the S2 attacker stays auxiliary to the leakage measures

citation: Jia (2026), HindsightBench: A Black-Box Behavioral Audit Protocol for Parametric Hindsight in Time-Indexed LLM Decision Tasks, arXiv 2607.18867 v2
text_source: 258 monthly US macro snapshots from ALFRED vintages, 2005-01 to 2026-06; no company text
feature: Date-trigger effect, transplant effect, post-cutoff placebo, date recovery, black-box recall propensity (20 samples at temperature 1.0), effective cutoff, recall-by-signal interaction
method: Four prompt arms that differ only in dating information (revealed, date-only, masked, wrong date) plus two memory probes; paired bootstrap; 15 models from seven vendors; pre-registered, with a reporting condition per metric
outcome: Crisis-minus-calm share of bearish direction calls; recalled outcome direction
incremental_to: Date-minus-masked contrast on post-cutoff dates as placebo (-0.073 to +0.066); Claude Sonnet 5 date trigger +0.326 [0.19, 0.46] and transplant +0.450 [0.26, 0.64]
pit_handling: Subject of the paper: measured cutoffs span 22 months and run up to eight months before vendor dates; recall, date recovery and behavioural use dissociate; masking gives a lower bound; results move with quantisation, reasoning mode, temperature and parser
informs_decision: S2 leakage measures: arm design, transplant control, recall probe protocol and its conditions; test-after-cutoff

citation: Wu, Cai and Wang (2026), MemTrial: Learning When to Trust Memory in LLM Portfolio Agents, arXiv 2610.11732 v2
text_source: Prices and news headlines for PortBench (99 assets), InvestorBench (4 stocks) and ClassAlloc (5 asset classes), 2015 to 2026; LLM-written lessons
feature: Counterfactual contribution of each stored experience; date-only numeric recall correlated with realised returns before and after the cutoff
method: Eight drafts per decision over a half-fraction factorial of four retrieved experiences; within-date contrast; hierarchical pooling; forward trust test; anchor at equal weight; 14 baselines; dates-hidden rerun
outcome: Investor utility net of 15 bp costs
incremental_to: Equal-weight portfolio: no LLM method beats it on PortBench or InvestorBench; trust test passes on at most 0.6% of decisions there
pit_handling: Limitation with two checks: recall 0.10 to 0.63 before the cutoff and -0.16 to +0.09 after; memory-free draft +0.082 pp before and -0.082 after for gpt-4.1-mini (p = 0.36); hiding dates leaves the gap
informs_decision: S2-d learning loop (within-episode contrast, trust test, rule fallback); recall probe scoring; factorial layout for multi-view runs

citation: Benhenda (2026), Look-Ahead-Bench: a Standardized Benchmark of Look-ahead Bias in Point-in-Time LLMs for Finance, arXiv 2601.13770 v1
text_source: Price history for five large-cap US technology stocks; other agent inputs not specified
feature: Alpha decay: excess return over buy-and-hold after the cutoff minus before
method: AI Hedge Fund multi-agent framework with monthly rebalancing; Llama 3.1 8B and 70B, DeepSeek 3.2 and three proprietary point-in-time models; six rule baselines; one run each
outcome: Portfolio return in excess of buy-and-hold
incremental_to: Rule baselines shift by -10.78 to +9.94 pp between windows; standard LLMs by -15.25 to -21.77 pp; point-in-time models by +0.31 to +1.30 pp
pit_handling: Subject of the paper, measured only by performance decay across two windows (April to September 2021; July to December 2024); cutoffs taken as stated; no recall probe; no standard errors
informs_decision: Performance decay not adopted as an S2 leakage measure; test-after-cutoff as convention

citation: Roy, Misra, Singh and Roy (2026), MemGuard-Alpha: Limits of Membership Inference for Detecting and Filtering Memorization-Contaminated Signals in LLM-Based Financial Forecasting, arXiv 2603.26797 v2 (the arXiv listing names Roy and Roy only)
text_source: 42,800 templated prompts on 50 S&P 100 stocks, January 2019 to June 2024; Financial PhraseBank as reference corpus
feature: Five membership-inference scores from token log-probabilities; composite with temporal proximity; cross-model disagreement split
method: Seven open-weight models (124M to 7B); audit under five protocols, a fixed-date across-model test with within-model normalisation, near-cutoff windows; 17 strategies with symmetric 15 bp costs and block bootstrap
outcome: In-sample status by stated cutoff; next-day return, Sharpe ratio
incremental_to: Unfiltered ensemble Sharpe 0.22; CMMD 0.37 (bootstrap p = 0.016, paired p = 0.114); dropping the weakest model 0.38; no significant five-factor alpha
pit_handling: Subject of the paper: temporal feature gives AUC 1.000 by construction; raw scores reach AUC 0.99 at a fixed date and fall to 0.487 to 0.537 after within-model normalisation; TinyLlama 0.93 falls to 0.38 within three months of its cutoff
informs_decision: S2 leakage measures: do not use membership inference or cross-model disagreement; validity checks for any measure (label circularity, within-model, near-cutoff)

citation: Ye, Han, Hu and seven others (2026), The Alpha Illusion: Reported Alpha from LLM Trading Agents Should Not Be Treated as Deployment Evidence, arXiv 2605.16895 v1
text_source: none (position paper; one reproduction on five tickers)
feature: Six reporting protocols P1 to P6; view-flip rate under reverse evidence
method: Review and argument; reproduction of TradingAgents and QuantAgent for 2025-01 to 2026-01 with commission, token cost, spread and market impact
outcome: Portfolio value and Sharpe ratio, gross and net
incremental_to: Buy-and-hold $104.8K against TradingAgents $102.3K net and QuantAgent $77.9K net; Sharpe 0.43 to 0.22 and -0.96 to -1.15 after costs
pit_handling: Post-cutoff evaluation as a minimum requirement; asks for retrieval-corpus timestamps and memory-update rules to be reported; no probe; backbone model of the reproduction not stated
informs_decision: Prior-tilt confound and dose-response check for counterfactual edits; memory-update reporting rule for S2-d; LLM as extractor with code doing the arithmetic

citation: Li, Zeng, Xing, Xu and Xu (2025), Profit Mirage: Revisiting Information Leakage in LLM-based Financial Agents, arXiv 2510.07920 v1
text_source: Prices and news for six assets (Yahoo Finance, Alpaca), 2020 to June 2025; 2,000 recall questions on January 2022 to June 2023
feature: Prediction consistency, confidence invariance and input dependency under input perturbation; closed-book recall accuracy
method: LLM writes strategy code, refined by tree search and a counterfactual simulator that minimises the leakage metrics; the code takes the decisions
outcome: Total return, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown; decay from a pre-cutoff to a post-cutoff window
incremental_to: Nine LLM agent baselines and buy and hold; no interval
pit_handling: Test window after GPT-4o's stated October 2023 cutoff; existing agents lose 50% to 72% of return past the cutoff; counterfactual samples carry no label
informs_decision: Strategy E (supported in direction, weak evidence); perturbation consistency is not a leakage metric without a should-change control; counterfactual edits measure sensitivity only

citation: Li, Wang and Ma (2026), Summoning the Oracle to Slay It: Mitigating Look-Ahead Bias in Financial Backtesting with Large Language Models, arXiv 2605.24564 v2
text_source: Price-derived summaries for seven US stocks and SPY; no text
feature: Logit contrast between the full prompt and a memory-activating prompt holding only entity and date, weighted by an entropy probe
method: Context-aware decoding with per-entity, per-date strength; eleven open models of 7B to 14B
outcome: Backtest ending value and Sharpe; rank correlation of the in-sample with the post-cutoff leaderboard
incremental_to: Unmitigated prompt, ticker anonymisation, stronger instruction (Spearman 0.779, 0.547, 0.482 against 0.846)
pit_handling: Post-cutoff window is the reference; needs next-token logits; black-box variants named and not evaluated
informs_decision: Strategy G stays a hypothesis for a commercial model; instruction-only and name-only anonymisation contradicted; correct only where a closed-book probe shows memory (C with G)

citation: Merchant and Levy (2025), A Fast and Effective Solution to the Problem of Look-ahead Bias in LLMs, arXiv 2512.06607 v2
text_source: MUSE news; 41 M&A deals from SDC (2010 to 2024); reports on two airlines
feature: Large-model logits shifted by the difference between two small models, one tuned on text to forget and one on text to retain
method: Divergence decoding, linear and rank forms; Gemma 3 27B with two Gemma 3 4B models
outcome: Rate of naming the true acquisition target; portfolio choice; MMLU
incremental_to: Unmodified model; unlearning baselines shown only in figures
pit_handling: Recall measured directly; no post-cutoff test; needs token-level logits; no black-box variant
informs_decision: Strategy G not available with a commercial API; recall-set selection rule (3 of 4 against 1 of 4) reusable for strategy C

citation: Gençay (2026), What survives honest evaluation? Leakage-safe, search-aware assessment of LLM-driven trading strategy discovery, arXiv 2608.27734 v1
text_source: Daily bars for 453 US large caps (2015 to 2026) and 39 ETFs (2005 to 2026); no text
feature: Declarative strategy plans composed by the LLM from a validated feature registry
method: Mechanical backtest; trial ledger; Deflated Sharpe Ratio; probability of backtest overfitting; planted leaky oracle
outcome: Evaluation-window Sharpe and its deflated value
horizon: Design 2017 to 2021 and evaluation 2022 to 2025 (stocks); 2007 to 2016 and 2017 to 2025 (ETFs)
incremental_to: Buy and hold, time-series momentum, a human rule system
pit_handling: Forward-looking features cannot be selected; model cutoffs and memorisation not addressed
informs_decision: Strategy E: closed rule vocabulary, trial ledger and stopping rule; statistics do not detect leakage; every LLM-discovered strategy was rejected

citation: Ghosh (2026), Frontier Autolab: Organizational Memory, Adversarial Dissent and Temporal Leakage in Multi-Agent LLM Firms Across Fifty Years of Technological Change, arXiv 2609.36739 v1
text_source: Judge-written era briefings, 1990 to 2040; no company filings
feature: A playbook of lessons appended after each revealed outcome and cited in later memos
method: Four exploratory runs of a simulated firm; the same model plays and judges; no ablation
outcome: Judge-assigned decision score and hindsight subscore
horizon: Nine eras, six scored against history
pit_handling: Defines leakage through weights and briefing-selection leakage; scores rise as the hindsight subscore falls (within-run r = -0.58); cutoffs not stated
informs_decision: Strategy F: a lesson writer with hindsight contaminates the playbook; ablate the playbook and blind the lesson writer

citation: Zhang, Chen and Stadie (2026), All Leaks Count, Some Count More: Interpretable Temporal Contamination Detection in LLM Backtesting, arXiv 2602.17234 v1
text_source: Model rationales on 98 Supreme Court cases, 152 NBA contracts and 100 within-sector stock ranking questions (December 2019 to June 2020)
feature: Atomic claims in the rationale, labelled leaked or admissible and weighted by Shapley value
method: Claim extraction and dating; TimeSPEC verify-and-regenerate pipeline; Claude Sonnet 4 through the API
outcome: Shapley-weighted decision-critical leakage rate; Brier score, relative error, Spearman correlation
incremental_to: Superforecasting prompt and a temporal-hint prompt (stock leakage 0.171 and 0.034 against 0.001; Spearman 0.543 and 0.523 against 0.167)
pit_handling: Pre-cutoff tasks by design; leakage blocked at inference, not removed; the model's cutoff not stated
informs_decision: Adds strategy J: audit the rationale claim by claim and re-answer from admissible claims; within-period ranking still leaked (bears on D)

citation: Yu, Li, Chen, Jiang, Li, Zhang, Liu, Suchow and Khashanah (2023), FinMem: A Performance-Enhanced LLM Trading Agent with Layered Memory and Character Design, arXiv 2311.13743 v2
text_source: Daily news, 10-Q and 10-K for five US stocks
feature: Layered long-term memory with decay; immediate and extended reflection
method: Training phase writes realised next-day price moves into memory; test phase trades one share; GPT-4-Turbo
outcome: Cumulative return, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown
horizon: Train 17 August 2021 to 5 October 2022; test 6 October 2022 to 10 April 2023
incremental_to: Buy and hold, reinforcement-learning and LLM agents
pit_handling: Not addressed; model cutoffs not stated; risk setting and backbone chosen on test-period results
informs_decision: Strategy F: outcome-labelled memory is the open-book arm with no placebo; memory as a contamination channel stays a hypothesis

citation: Zhang, Zhao, Gao, You, Jia, Zhao, An and Sun (2026), AlphaForgeBench: Benchmarking End-to-End Trading Strategy Design with Large Language Models, arXiv 2602.18481 v2
text_source: 633 strategy queries from broker reports, factor libraries and publications; daily prices for two crypto pairs and five US stocks
method: Single generate-then-backtest pass on a deterministic engine; six commercial models
outcome: Annualised return, Sharpe and four other metrics
pit_handling: Not addressed in the part read; model cutoffs not stated; queries come from public sources
informs_decision: Strategy E: separating stochastic generation from deterministic execution makes scoring reproducible; no evidence on leakage

citation: Paleka, Sudhir, Alvarez, Bhat, Shen, Wang and Tramèr (2024), Consistency Checks for Language Model Forecasters, arXiv 2412.18544 v2
text_source: Binary forecasting questions from Metaculus, Manifold and news articles
feature: Violation of ten logical consistency checks across related forecasts, scored by arbitrage profit
method: Automated generation of question tuples; eight commercial and open models
outcome: Correlation of consistency violation with Brier score
incremental_to: MMLU error rate (correlation 0.38 and 0.55 with Brier)
pit_handling: Questions resolve after the forecasters' cutoffs, as the authors state; a 2028 set has no outcomes yet
informs_decision: Adds strategy K: an outcome-free signal (conditional checks correlate 0.92 and 0.71 with Brier); forcing consistency did not improve Brier, so use as a diagnostic only
